result.title: MENTOR: Learning from Failure with On-Policy Pedagogical Intervention
result.summary: Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is a key driver for Large Reasoning Models, but it is vulnerable to "zero-reward collapse", a training failure where a sudden increase in task difficulty causes the learning signal to vanish. We argue that the conventional approach of discarding these failed trajectories is wasteful, as they contain valuable diagnostic information about the model's cognitive gaps, a bright side that can be leveraged for recovery. Existing solutions, however, often regress to static, "off-policy-style" interventions like pre-defined hint libraries or perform post-hoc refinement, failing to provide the adaptive, forward-looking guidance needed to escape the collapse. To address this, we propose a paradigm shift towards on-policy pedagogical intervention and introduce MENTOR, a multi-agent framework that acts as a live mentor. MENTOR diagnoses the root cause of failure in real-time and dynamically generates targeted, instructional prompts to guide the learning agent's next attempt. As a plug-and-play module, MENTOR integrates seamlessly into existing policy optimization pipelines like GRPO without modifying the training infrastructure. Extensive experiments on math and code generation show that MENTOR effectively mitigates zero-reward collapse, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. Notably, it achieves massive average relative gains of up to 78.3% on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct over its base model.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 RLVR 训练中任务突然变难导致的「零奖励坍缩」，提出多智能体框架 MENTOR，实时诊断失败根因并动态生成教学式提示，以 on-policy 方式引导策略下一次尝试，可即插即用地嵌入 GRPO 等流程。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本训练侧工作，但其「失败轨迹含诊断信息 + on-policy 实时干预」的思路，可能为 latent 推理轨迹的监督与贡献分配、以及推理信号坍缩时的恢复提供可核查线索；与视觉状态表示无直接关系。
